recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No current FHIR core source edit is needed unless a future work group decision reintroduces an active DiagnosticOrder-like artifact with result-oriented aliases.
issue_request: FHIR-5284 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 OO ballot comment against the clinical table of contents asking to correct the DiagnosticOrder alias list because result/report/lab aliases described results rather than an order.
initial_application: No commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-5284 was found. Git history shows d6259fa8e3beda8fd5e58ad54d85001f1efb9d42 removed the stale result/lab alias cell from source/diagnosticorder/diagnosticorder-spreadsheet.xml while leaving those aliases on DiagnosticReport.
additional_context: DiagnosticOrder is listed as a removed resource and is commented as subsumed into ServiceRequest in current source/fhir.ini. Later Published issues FHIR-10295 and FHIR-11119 explain the rename/merge path out of the active resource set. Current ServiceRequest aliases are request/order oriented, and DiagnosticReport retains the report/lab aliases.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The original correction is already reflected in history and current active source has no DiagnosticOrder alias list carrying the stale result/lab wording.

related_jiras.note: Published/Persuasive rename of request resources from Order to Request explains why DiagnosticOrder left the active resource set.
Published/Persuasive merge of DiagnosticRequest and ProcedureRequest explains the path toward the current ServiceRequest successor.
